appraisal.condition_assessment: Case and wheel spokes appear complete and undamaged with typical brass patina/tarnish, not recently polished. Dial is clean and legible with matching hands present. Cannot confirm from photos whether the glass crystal is present/intact, whether the movement runs, keeps time, or strikes correctly, or whether the winding key is included — all of which materially affect price. No visible dents or missing spokes on the wheel.
appraisal.identified_item: Schatz German brass ship's wheel clock, 'Ship's Bell' model, 8-day, 7-jewel movement
appraisal.reasoning: Schatz ship's wheel/ship's bell clocks are a well-known and fairly common category among nautical collectors — genuinely by Schatz (marked 'Schatz Ships Bell, 8 Day, 7 Jewels, Made in Germany' on the dial, consistent with known production), not a reproduction. These generally trade in a modest but reliable band at auction/on eBay, roughly $100-300 depending on completeness (winding key), working/serviceable condition, and whether the bell-strike function (if this example has one) operates correctly — none of which is verifiable from photos alone. I do not have specific recalled realised sale records for this exact model to cite as comps, so I'm leaving comps empty rather than inventing figures, and holding confidence low as instructed. Current bidding ($56/8 bids, 43h left) is consistent with this landing in the $120-200 range at hammer, which is where I've centered the as-is estimate. This is an ordinary-condition example of a desirable but not rare maker/model — no exceptional finish, complication, or box/papers to push it higher.
appraisal.style_era: Mid-20th century nautical/maritime decor, likely 1950s-1970s West German manufacture

appraisal.identified_item: Oil painting on canvas, impressionist-style Mediterranean/villa courtyard garden scene with arched window, tile roof, and wrought-iron gate, in a gold composite frame
appraisal.maker_guess: Hung Pham (attributed per listing title; signature not clearly legible in photos)
appraisal.reasoning: This is a genuine hand-painted oil (visible brush/impasto texture in the florals and stucco, not a print), consistent with the decorative-impressionist villa/garden compositions commonly attributed to Hung Pham, a working artist whose similar courtyard/garden scenes circulate frequently through estate-auction channels including EBTH itself. However, I cannot recall specific, itemized realized auction results for Hung Pham with confidence (price/venue/size), so per instructions I'm not fabricating comps and am capping confidence at 0.4. From general pattern-of-market knowledge, this class of decorative estate-sale impressionist oil (unknown or minor-market named artist, garden/villa subject, ~24x30in with frame) typically hammers in the low hundreds of dollars at venues like EBTH — often $60-200 as-is, occasionally more for larger/stronger examples — well below gallery/retail ask prices for similarly attributed works. Current bidding at $30/5 bids is plausible early-stage activity for this tier of lot; I'd expect it to close somewhere in the $70-150 range. Valued as-is (unrestored, sold now); no restoration appears needed based on photos.
appraisal.style_era: Contemporary decorative Impressionist, late 20th century
